title: Perimeter and Area of Plane Shapes

blocks.text: A builder pricing a fence needs the perimeter. A builder pricing floor tiles needs the area. Confusing the two is an expensive mistake on a real site — and an easy one to make in an exam.

blocks.title: Perimeter and area
blocks.text: **Perimeter** is the total distance right round the boundary of a shape, measured in cm, m or km. **Area** is the amount of surface enclosed, measured in square units such as cm² or m².

blocks.caption: The six formulas that cover almost every WAEC mensuration question

blocks.markdown:
### Height must be perpendicular

In the triangle and parallelogram formulas, **height** means the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex or side. It is not the slanted side.

Using a slant length instead of the perpendicular height is one of the most common errors in this topic, and it always gives an answer that is too large.

blocks.caption: Area and circumference of a circle — note area uses the radius squared

blocks.title: Circle calculations with π = 22/7
blocks.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm and the area of a circle of radius 14 cm, taking π = 22/7.

steps.text: For the circumference, use C = 2πr with r = 7.
The 7 cancels neatly with the denominator.
For the area, use A = πr² with r = 14. Square the radius first.

blocks.title: When to use 22/7
blocks.text: Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ whenever the radius or diameter is a multiple of 7, because the 7s cancel and you get an exact answer. Otherwise $\pi = 3.142$ is usually easier. Always use the value the question specifies.

blocks.markdown:
### Composite shapes

For an L-shape or a shape with a piece removed, split it into rectangles, triangles and parts of circles. Then **add** the areas of the pieces, or **subtract** the area of the hole.

Be careful with the perimeter of a composite shape: some internal edges are not part of the boundary at all, so they must not be counted.

items: 1 hectare = 10 000 m², the unit used for farmland.
Convert all lengths to the same unit before calculating, never afterwards.

blocks.title: Squaring the conversion factor
blocks.text: Converting area is not the same as converting length. Since 1 m = 100 cm, you might expect 1 m² = 100 cm², but it is actually 10 000 cm² — the factor gets squared because area has two dimensions.

points: Perimeter is a length; area is a surface measured in square units.
Use the perpendicular height, never the slant side, in triangle and parallelogram areas.
The area of a circle uses $r^2$ while the circumference uses $r$.
Take $\pi = 22/7$ when the radius is a multiple of 7, otherwise 3.142.
Split composite shapes into simple pieces and add or subtract their areas.
When converting area units, square the length conversion factor.
